## SEO Audit Checklist Before Hiring an Agency

Use an SEO audit checklist before hiring an agency to understand your website’s actual problems, separate essential work from optional recommendations, and compare agencies on evidence rather than promises. A useful audit should review technical SEO, content, search visibility, local search, links, analytics and business goals—not just produce a long list of software errors.

Hiring an SEO agency without checking its audit process can lead to unclear deliverables, unsuitable keywords, unnecessary website changes or a focus on rankings that does not generate relevant enquiries. This checklist is designed for Indian small businesses, NGOs, schools, clinics, D2C brands and agencies evaluating an SEO partner.

## Why an SEO Audit Matters Before Agency Selection

An SEO audit is a structured review of how easily search engines can discover, understand and evaluate your website. It should also examine whether the website is useful to the people you want to reach.

For example, a clinic in Pune may need to appear for location-based searches and provide clear information about doctors, treatments, fees, appointment methods and the clinic’s address. A D2C brand may need stronger product pages, useful category pages, structured product information and a clean buying journey. An NGO may be more concerned with visibility for its programmes, donation-related searches, volunteer recruitment and trust signals.

These are different SEO problems. An agency that recommends the same checklist for every website may not understand your business.

### What an audit should help you decide

A good audit should help answer questions such as:

- Can search engines crawl and index the important pages?
- Are the pages targeting searches that your customers or supporters actually use?
- Does each important page have a clear purpose?
- Are technical problems preventing visibility?
- Is the content accurate, useful and suitable for Indian users?
- Are local search listings complete and consistent?
- Are website visitors taking meaningful actions?
- Which improvements should happen first?
- What work should your internal team handle, and what requires agency support?

The audit should not be treated as a one-time certificate that makes a website “SEO ready”. SEO is an ongoing process because competitors, search results, customer behaviour, website content and search engine systems change.

### A report is not the same as a strategy

Many SEO tools can automatically identify missing title tags, broken links, slow pages and other issues. That information can be useful, but it is not a complete strategy.

A strategy explains the business impact of a problem, its priority, the recommended action, who will implement it and how success will be assessed. It also considers limitations such as your website platform, available content resources, approval processes and budget.

## SEO Audit Checklist: Information to Prepare

Before speaking to agencies, collect basic information about your business and website. This allows agencies to assess the right issues instead of making assumptions.

### Business and audience details

Prepare a short brief covering:

- Your main products, services or programmes
- The locations you serve
- Your most profitable or important offerings
- Your preferred customer types
- The languages your audience uses
- Your main competitors, including offline competitors
- The action you want visitors to take
- Seasonal periods that affect demand
- Current marketing channels
- Any words, services or locations you do not want to target

For an Indian business, language and location can be particularly important. Your audience may search in English, Hindi, Marathi or a combination of languages. Do not assume that translating English pages word for word will automatically create effective regional-language content. The wording should reflect how the intended audience searches and understands the service.

### Website and access details

An agency may request access to:

- Google Search Console
- Google Analytics or another analytics platform
- Google Business Profile
- Your content management system
- Your hosting or technical contact
- Your tag management system
- Your paid advertising accounts, if relevant
- Your CRM, enquiry system or ecommerce platform

Do not share personal passwords. Use individual user access with suitable permissions, and remove access when a contract ends. Keep ownership of your domain, hosting, Google accounts, analytics property, Search Console property and business profile with your organisation.

If an agency asks to create these assets under its own email address, ask why. Losing access to core accounts can create serious problems during a change of agency.

### Existing performance information

Collect available data for a useful comparison period. The exact period depends on the website’s traffic and seasonality, but it should be long enough to reveal normal patterns rather than one unusual week.

Look for:

- Organic clicks and impressions
- Search queries and pages receiving traffic
- Enquiries, calls, form submissions or purchases
- Branded and non-branded search activity
- Top landing pages
- Pages with high traffic but few enquiries
- Pages with enquiries but low visibility
- Major website changes
- Previous SEO work
- Manual actions or security issues shown in Search Console

An agency should explain what the data can and cannot show. For example, traffic alone does not prove business value. A smaller number of relevant visitors can be more useful than a large number of visitors who are unlikely to become customers.

## Technical SEO Audit Checklist

Technical SEO concerns the website’s ability to be accessed, crawled, understood and displayed. It also overlaps with user experience and website maintenance.

### Crawlability and indexation

Ask the agency to check:

- Whether important pages can be crawled
- Whether important pages are included in the index
- Whether robots.txt is blocking useful content
- Whether the XML sitemap contains the right URLs
- Whether the sitemap is submitted and updated
- Whether pages have accidental noindex instructions
- Whether duplicate versions of pages exist
- Whether redirects are working correctly
- Whether deleted or moved pages return appropriate responses
- Whether internal links lead to important pages
- Whether orphan pages exist without internal links

A website may have many URLs but only a smaller group may deserve search visibility. Filter pages, internal search results, tag pages and technical variations can create unnecessary duplication. The agency should explain which pages should be indexed and why.

### Site structure and internal linking

Review whether the website structure matches the way people look for your offerings. A service business might organise content by service and location. A school may need sections for admissions, curriculum, facilities, notices and contact information. A D2C site may need clear category, product, collection and informational pages.

Internal links should help users and search engines reach important pages. Check whether:

- Main services are linked from relevant pages
- Blog posts link to useful service or product pages
- Important pages are not buried several clicks deep
- Link text describes the destination accurately
- Navigation works on mobile devices
- Breadcrumbs are useful where the site structure is complex

Avoid an agency that recommends adding large numbers of exact-match keyword links without considering readability. Internal linking should support navigation, not make pages appear artificially optimised.

### Mobile experience and page performance

A technical audit should review mobile usability and performance, since many Indian users browse through mobile networks and smartphones. Check:

- Whether text can be read without excessive zooming
- Whether buttons and forms are easy to use
- Whether menus work on smaller screens
- Whether pop-ups block the main content
- Whether images are appropriately sized
- Whether scripts and third-party tools slow down key pages
- Whether pages remain usable on less reliable connections
- Whether checkout, enquiry and appointment journeys work on mobile

Performance scores from tools are indicators, not the complete user experience. Ask the agency to identify the templates or page types that matter most and explain what changes are practical on your platform.

### Security, redirects and website stability

The audit should check whether the website uses HTTPS correctly and whether old HTTP versions redirect properly. It should also identify redirect chains, broken redirects, mixed-content warnings and unnecessary technical variations.

For an ecommerce website, the agency should be careful with product availability, discontinued products, filters, pagination and checkout URLs. For a clinic or school, forms and appointment pages should be reviewed for reliability and privacy.

SEO agencies are not a replacement for a security specialist. If the audit identifies malware, data exposure or a compromised website, treat that as a separate urgent technical matter.

## On-Page SEO and Content Checklist

Technical fixes cannot compensate for pages that do not answer the audience’s questions or match the service being offered.

### Search intent and keyword suitability

Ask how the agency chooses keywords. It should consider:

- What the searcher is trying to do
- Whether the search relates to information, comparison, purchase or local service
- Whether your business genuinely satisfies that intent
- Whether the search is relevant to your location
- Whether the phrase has commercial value for your organisation
- Whether the competition is realistic for your current website
- Whether variations in Indian spelling or language matter

Keyword volume should not be the only selection criterion. A phrase may have visible search demand but attract people who are not suitable customers. Another phrase may have limited demand but lead to valuable enquiries.

The agency should map selected topics to specific pages. If several pages target the same intent, the result may be internal competition and unclear page purpose.

### Page-level review

For important pages, review:

- Page title
- Main heading
- Subheadings
- Introduction
- Service or product details
- Benefits and limitations
- Pricing or quotation information where appropriate
- Calls to action
- Contact information
- Images and alternative text
- Internal links
- Meta description
- Frequently asked questions
- Trust and credibility information

Titles and descriptions should accurately describe the page rather than repeat keywords. A page title that promises one service while the page discusses another creates a poor experience and may reduce qualified clicks.

For Indian buyers, practical details often matter. Depending on the business, pages may need information about service areas, delivery locations, GST invoices, payment methods, warranty, return rules, appointment process, language support and customer support channels.

### Content quality and editorial control

Ask whether the agency will:

- Improve existing pages before creating new ones
- Provide outlines or complete drafts
- Use subject matter input from your team
- Fact-check health, education, finance or legal content
- Follow your brand tone
- Avoid copied or lightly rewritten content
- Review old pages for accuracy
- Maintain a content calendar connected to business priorities

For clinics, health information should be reviewed by a suitably qualified professional. For schools, information about admissions, results and facilities must be current. For NGOs, programme claims, impact statements and donation information should be accurate and responsibly presented.

AI tools may assist with research or drafting, but the agency should explain its review process. Publishing large quantities of generic content can create maintenance work without serving users.

### Structured data and rich results

Structured data can help search engines interpret certain types of information, such as products, organisations, local businesses, articles, events or FAQs. It does not guarantee enhanced search results.

Ask the agency to use structured data only where it accurately represents visible page content and complies with current search engine guidance. It should also explain how the markup will be tested and maintained.

## Local SEO, Links and Measurement Checklist

### Local SEO for Indian businesses

If you serve a city, neighbourhood or specific service area, local SEO should be part of the audit. Review:

- Google Business Profile completeness
- Business name, address and phone consistency
- Primary and secondary categories
- Service descriptions
- Opening hours and holiday hours
- Website and appointment links
- Photos and updates
- Customer reviews and responses
- Duplicate listings
- Location pages
- Local contact information
- Directions and accessibility details

Do not create multiple fake locations to target nearby areas. Location pages should represent genuine service coverage and provide useful, distinct information.

Review platforms may matter differently by industry. A restaurant, clinic, school, home-service provider and B2B agency may need different local visibility approaches. The agency should recommend platforms based on how your audience chooses providers, not simply provide a standard directory list.

Reviews should be requested honestly and handled according to platform policies. An agency should not promise a particular review rating or offer incentives that could violate platform rules.

### Backlink and off-page review

Backlinks are links from other websites to your website. A useful audit reviews the quality, relevance and context of existing links rather than counting them alone.

Ask the agency to check:

- Links from relevant industry or community websites
- Links to important pages
- Suspicious or clearly manipulative patterns
- Links created through directories or networks
- Mentions without links
- Digital PR or partnership opportunities
- Competitor visibility patterns

Be cautious if an agency sells a fixed number of backlinks every month without explaining where they will come from. Mass directory submissions, private link networks, irrelevant guest posts and paid links that violate search engine policies can create risk.

Do not assume every low-quality link requires immediate removal. Ask for evidence that a link is harmful and why a particular action is recommended.

### Analytics and conversion measurement

The audit should connect search visibility to useful actions. Depending on your organisation, this might include:

- Calls
- WhatsApp enquiries
- Contact form submissions
- Appointment requests
- Brochure downloads
- Product purchases
- Donation completions
- Volunteer applications
- School admission enquiries
- Newsletter registrations

Tracking should respect consent and applicable privacy requirements. For websites serving users in India, discuss how personal data is collected, stored, shared and retained. Avoid sending sensitive personal details into analytics tools unless the setup is designed and permitted for that purpose.

Ask whether the agency will distinguish between:

- Organic traffic and other traffic sources
- First-time and returning users
- Branded and non-branded searches
- Leads and qualified leads
- Online enquiries and completed sales
- Vanity metrics and business outcomes

## How to Evaluate the Agency’s Audit

Once agencies submit audits or proposals, compare the thinking behind them.

| Evaluation area | What a strong agency should show | Warning sign |
|---|---|---|
| Business understanding | Recommendations linked to your services, audience and locations | Generic findings that could apply to any website |
| Technical review | Prioritised issues with examples, impact and implementation notes | A long automated error list without context |
| Keyword research | Intent, relevance, competition and page mapping | Promises based only on search volume |
| Content plan | Clear topics, page purpose, quality control and internal inputs | Large quantities of generic articles |
| Local SEO | Profile, reviews, location and service-area recommendations | Fake locations or guaranteed map positions |
| Link strategy | Relevant, transparent and policy-aware methods | Fixed backlink quantities with unclear sources |
| Measurement | Defined conversions and reporting method | Traffic and rankings presented as the only outcomes |
| Communication | Named responsibilities, meeting rhythm and approval process | Vague claims that “the team will handle everything” |
| Access and ownership | Your organisation retains account and website ownership | Agency-controlled accounts or unclear handover |
| Commercial clarity | Scope, exclusions, GST treatment and renewal terms are explained | Low headline fee with many undisclosed extras |

### Ask for prioritisation

Every finding should ideally have a priority such as urgent, high, medium or low. However, labels alone are not enough.

Ask the agency:

- What happens if this issue is not fixed?
- How many important pages are affected?
- Is the issue confirmed or only a tool recommendation?
- Can it be fixed without a redesign?
- Who will make the change?
- How will the change be checked?
- What depends on another task?

This helps you avoid spending the first few months on minor metadata changes while major problems with content, conversion paths or indexation remain unresolved.

### Request a sample of the working process

You do not need to demand a complete free audit from every agency. Instead, ask for a short explanation or sample showing how it would approach one important page.

For example, request:

- The likely user intent for the page
- The page’s current problem
- One or two recommended changes
- The required input from your team
- How the agency would measure the effect

This reveals more than a decorative presentation. It also prevents agencies from doing extensive unpaid work during the selection process.

### Check communication and implementation capability

Some agencies can identify issues but cannot implement them. Others can make technical changes but have limited content or strategic capability.

Clarify whether the agency will:

- Make changes directly
- Provide instructions to your developer
- Write and upload content
- Manage approvals
- Coordinate with your hosting provider
- Handle multilingual content
- Work with Shopify, WordPress, WooCommerce or another platform
- Support website migrations or redesigns

If your website is maintained by a Pune-based developer, an internal IT person or a separate vendor, include that person in the implementation discussion. SEO recommendations that cannot be deployed are not useful, however accurate they may be.

## Red Flags Before Signing an SEO Contract

Be cautious about guarantees such as “number one on Google”, a fixed ranking for competitive terms or a fixed volume of leads. Search performance depends on many factors outside an agency’s control, including competition, website quality, search behaviour, location and industry conditions.

Other warning signs include:

- No questions about your business or customers
- A proposal based only on domain authority or a single audit score
- Unusually large promises without a baseline
- No explanation of what the client must provide
- Unclear ownership of content and accounts
- Content copied from competitors
- Recommendations to hide text or create doorway pages
- Mass backlink packages
- Fake reviews or fake business locations
- Reports that show rankings but not conversions
- Automatic renewals or lock-in clauses that are difficult to understand
- No process for handling website changes
- No explanation of GST, invoices or payment terms

A professional agency should be comfortable discussing uncertainty. It can explain what it plans to improve, what evidence it will monitor and what factors may affect the outcome without guaranteeing a ranking.

## What the Proposal and Contract Should Cover

Before appointment, ensure the proposal clearly states:

- The audit scope
- The websites, subdomains or locations included
- Technical SEO responsibilities
- Content responsibilities
- Local SEO activities
- Link-building or digital PR activities
- Analytics and tracking work
- Reporting frequency
- Meeting and communication channels
- Approval responsibilities
- Expected deliverables
- Exclusions
- GST treatment
- Payment schedule
- Minimum term and notice period
- Account and asset ownership
- Data handling expectations
- Handover process after termination

The agency may recommend a redesign, migration or platform change. Ask whether the SEO work includes migration planning, URL mapping, redirects, staging checks and post-launch monitoring. A redesign can affect search visibility even when the new design appears better.

Do not approve every recommendation at once. Start with the work that addresses important business and user problems. A practical roadmap may include technical fixes, improvements to high-value pages, local profile work, conversion tracking and a realistic content plan.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What should an SEO audit include before hiring an agency?

It should include technical SEO, indexation, site structure, mobile usability, page performance, keyword intent, content quality, internal linking, local search, backlinks, analytics and conversion tracking. It should also prioritise the findings and connect them to your business goals. A tool-generated score without recommendations and implementation context is not enough.

### Can I complete an SEO audit myself?

You can complete an initial review using Google Search Console, analytics, page checks and a manual review of important pages. A technical specialist may still be needed for complex JavaScript, migrations, ecommerce issues, international or multilingual websites and server-level problems. A self-review is useful for agency selection because it helps you ask better questions.

### Should I choose an agency that promises first-page rankings?

No. A promise of a particular ranking is not a reliable basis for agency selection. Ask how the agency will choose relevant search topics, improve pages, measure qualified enquiries and report on progress. Search visibility should be assessed alongside business outcomes and the quality of traffic.

### How often should an SEO audit be performed?

The frequency depends on the size and complexity of the website and how often it changes. A small brochure website may need a detailed review less often than an ecommerce site with frequent product changes. Technical monitoring and Search Console checks should happen more regularly, especially after a redesign, migration or major content update.

### Should an SEO agency also manage Google Ads?

Not necessarily. SEO and Google Ads require different planning, although the data can sometimes support both channels. Choose an agency based on the capability you need, and ensure paid advertising costs, account ownership and campaign management are clearly separated from SEO work.

### How much does an SEO audit cost in India?

The cost depends on the website’s size, platform, number of locations, ecommerce complexity, language requirements and depth of analysis. A basic review is different from a technical audit with implementation support and conversion analysis. Ask for a written scope, GST treatment and clear exclusions rather than comparing only a headline fee.

## Where to Start

Prepare your business brief, collect access safely, list your most important pages and write down the actions that matter most, such as calls, WhatsApp enquiries, sales, donations or admission requests. Use this SEO audit checklist to compare at least a few agencies on evidence, prioritisation, implementation ability, reporting and account ownership.
